title: Lord! That I May Learn of Thee
description: Lord! That I May Learn of Thee in Tonic Solfa to VIENNA, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 505 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Simplicity of Christ”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to VIENNA; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord! that I may learn of thee, Give me true sim-plic-i-ty; Wean my soul, and keep it low, Will-ing thee a-lone to know.

lines: Lord! that I may learn of thee,
Wean my soul, and keep it low,

licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to VIENNA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
